title: Large PaaS vendors bundle MCP-identity gateway into default platform by H1 2027
body: Snowflake stacked three pre-Summit catalysts inside the May 27-29 window: a $6B five-year AWS Graviton commitment (2.4x the 2023 deal), a definitive agreement to acquire Natoma for identity-aware Model Context Protocol gateway capabilities at the individual tool-call level, and a Q1 FY27 earnings beat with raised 31% product-revenue guidance, heading into the Monday June 1 Summit 26 keynote at Moscone where CEO Sridhar Ramaswamy shares the stage with Anthropic President Daniela Amodei in front of a projected 20,000+ in-person attendees. The stock gapped 36% Thursday on the print and added 6.88% Friday to close near $255, the largest two-day rally in the stock's public history. The structural force is mechanical: once one major data/AI PaaS vendor bundles MCP-identity-gateway capabilities directly into its default platform with a public acquisition price tag and a keynote demo, every peer PaaS vendor faces a procurement-side question that arrives in customer RFPs within one purchase cycle, namely whether the platform enforces identity, policy, and audit at the individual MCP tool-call level natively, or whether the customer has to stitch a third-party gateway in front of it. The named cohort under pressure: Databricks (Data + AI Summit June 15-18 at the same Moscone complex), Cloudera, Salesforce Data Cloud + Agentforce, Microsoft Fabric and the Windows Agent Framework drop at Build June 2-3, Google BigQuery + Vertex AI, and Confluent. The forcing function is that enterprise AI-governance buyers (the same procurement teams writing the NIST AI RMF and EU AI Act compliance perimeter) refuse to map N vendor-specific MCP-identity stacks into N risk-acceptance frameworks, the same coordination pressure that converged hyperscaler IAM templates and SBOM formats. By H1 2027 we expect at least two of the named PaaS vendors to ship publicly-disclosed M&A or first-party announcements adding MCP-identity gateway capabilities (per-tool-call identity, policy, and audit) to their default platform tier, not a paid add-on, not a partner-marketplace listing. Bear case is a Snowflake-Natoma integration-quality stumble that erodes the reference-point status before peer PaaS commitments land; absent that stumble, H1 2027 lands MCP-identity gateway as a default-platform category line item across the major data/AI PaaS vendor cohort.

reasoning.because: Snowflake bundles MCP-identity gateway via Natoma acquisition + +44% two-day stock rip pre-Summit
reasoning.given: Databricks, Microsoft Fabric, Salesforce, BigQuery, Vertex AI face same RFP question one cycle out
reasoning.so_that: >=2 named PaaS vendors ship publicly-disclosed M&A or first-party MCP-identity gateways in default platform tier
reasoning.landing: By H1 2027; two named PaaS vendors ship default-tier MCP-identity gateway
reasoning.plain_language: Snowflake just bought a tool that controls which AI agents touch what. Other big data platforms will copy it within a year.

summary: Snowflake stacked a $6B AWS Graviton commit, a Natoma MCP-identity-gateway acquisition, and a Q1 FY27 beat into May 27-29, gapping +44% pre-Summit. By H1 2027 >=2 of Databricks, Microsoft Fabric, Salesforce, BigQuery, Vertex AI ship default-tier MCP-identity gateways.
